title: EXP-023 — Additional Web Designer Launch While Retaining Existing Client
objective: Test one new capability only: whether exactly one activation of the supported Web Client Designer-launch UI route creates a distinct additional rendered Web Designer client while the original Designer and authenticated Web Client remain open and their inherited Form/dialog state is preserved. Establish a visible/browser client baseline, attempt that launch once, and distinguish a new rendered client from focusing/reusing the existing one. Normal User editing-scope confirmation in a newly created Designer is part of the launch procedure. Do not create or modify any Mongoose artifact, change Caption or another Form property, Save, close/reopen a Form, close an existing client, or establish authentication. This is a prerequisite observation for a possible later Caption experiment, not a Caption recovery or persistence test and not proof of distinct backend sessions, cache eviction, or database access.

in_scope: Read EXP-009 and EXP-009-R2 for the supported Web Client Designer-launch UI route, and EXP-021-R4 and EXP-022 for inherited-state context; their original Designer-close procedure is not part of EXP-023
Read-only preflight establishing a usable already-authenticated Web Client, a visibly open original Designer with User editing scope, and browser tab/window identities before the launch attempt

Before launch, visibly establish that the authenticated Web Client has no currently open/active Mongoose Form, judging its normal rendered runtime Form tabs/content. If a Form is open or that prerequisite cannot be established, stop blocked without closing it, clearing state, reloading, navigating or otherwise manufacturing the prerequisite
Record the original Designer's visible Form tabs, selected Form, dirty-state indicators and dialogs without changing them; do not investigate any prior experiment's blocked property or editor
Exactly one activation of the existing Web Client Designer-launch UI command used in EXP-009/R2, while retaining the original Designer and authenticated Web Client
Observe whether that one activation creates a distinct additional rendered Designer client or merely focuses/reuses the existing client; record an error or ambiguous result without retrying
In a newly created Designer only, perform normal User editing-scope confirmation if the supported launch flow requires it; this is not authentication or a User Preference change
Record the additional Designer's rendered initial Form tabs/dialogs and User scope without opening a Form or inferring hidden inventory or backend identity

Read-only post-launch comparison confirming the original Designer and Web Client remain present and inherited visible Form/dialog and dirty state has not been saved, discarded, closed or otherwise changed
Capture inspected before/after screenshots and browser client evidence under evidence/EXP-023/, identifying observations and what remains unproven
Write only the new EXP-023 record and evidence/EXP-023/; reconcile one launch-command activation and zero Mongoose artifact mutations or authentication actions
out_of_scope: Form Caption, Description or component-property changes, recovery or persistence testing
Creating, modifying, saving, deleting, renaming, opening or closing any Mongoose Form or component
Continuation, retry, cleanup, workaround or investigation of EXP-021-R4 or EXP-022
Closing the original Designer, replacing or restarting the Web Client, or repeating/substituting the launch route
Authentication, Sign In, session establishment, User Preferences changes, Regenerate, explicit unload, cache clearing or stronger lifecycle operations
Form variables, FormSync, IDO metadata, bindings, scripts, event handlers, validators, collections or data-source work
Proving a distinct backend, Portal, Web Client, Designer backend or IDO Runtime session, internal object identity, database durability or cache eviction
Claiming Caption recovery is established by a successful launch observation or promoting this first execution to replay_verified

prohibited_actions: Create, modify, save, delete or rename any Mongoose artifact, including an FX_ artifact; no artifact mutation is authorized by EXP-023
Open, close or reopen a Mongoose Form or continue an inherited creation/property-edit dialog
Save, discard, close, delete or modify inherited dirty Forms or uncommitted dialogs; stop blocked if the launch cannot preserve them
Close the original Designer or replace, restart, reload or close the existing authenticated Web Client
Activate Designer launch while the authenticated Web Client has a currently open/active Mongoose Form or that state remains ambiguous; stop blocked without closing or changing inherited state
Close, manipulate or continue any Form unexpectedly appearing in the additional Designer; capture the observed result and stop blocked
Activate the Web Client Designer-launch command more than once or use an alternate launch route after focus/reuse, error or ambiguity
Perform authentication, Sign In, reauthentication or session establishment at any point; if an existing client is unusable or a new launch requests authentication, stop blocked
Invoke explicit unload, Regenerate Form, cache clearing or User Preferences changes
Investigate No Colon or another previous experiment's unresolved property/editor
Use hidden/internal representations, browser JavaScript evaluation or manipulation as a substitute for rendered client and scope evidence
Blindly repeat an interrupted browser or shell action; one fresh snapshot and one corrected read-only inspection may clarify the result, but do not repeat launch or any dialog submission
Modify production data, weaken security, or read, print, log or expose credential values
Start another experiment, claim Caption persistence or backend-session independence, or promote this single observation to replay_verified
prohibited_patterns: \b(launch|open|create)\b[^.\n]{0,50}\b(more than one|two|three|multiple|second additional|another additional)\b[^.\n]{0,40}\b(web designer|designer client)s?\b

environment.notes: Requires usable existing authenticated Web Client and original Designer before the single launch attempt. Preserve inherited dirty state. Authentication restoration or cleanup is outside this experiment. Before launch, rendered evidence must establish no currently open/active Form in the authenticated Web Client; if a Form is open or state is ambiguous, stop blocked without cleanup.

acceptance_checks.description: Before the launch attempt, record the original Designer and authenticated Web Client browser tab/window identities. Visibly establish that both are usable, that the original Designer shows User editing scope, and that no blocking authentication or error dialog prevents the supported launch. Stop blocked if preflight is unusable; do not restore authentication or repair the environment under EXP-023. Before any launch, visibly establish that the authenticated Web Client has no currently open/active Mongoose Form using its rendered runtime Form tabs/content. A dialog, unrelated Portal surface or URL alone does not establish this prerequisite. If a Form is open or the state cannot be established, stop blocked without closing it, reloading, navigating or changing inherited state to manufacture the prerequisite.

Capture and inspect an inherited-state baseline: original Designer visible Form tabs, selected Form, scope, dirty-state indicators and dialogs; Web Client visible state; and current Designer client count/identities. Identify any inherited dirty or uncommitted state and preserve it. Do not open another Form, change a property, clear a filter or dismiss an inherited dialog for cleanup. The inspected Web Client baseline screenshot and observations must explicitly support the rendered no-currently-open/active-Form guard from AC-1, and record any uncertainty rather than assuming it from a missing label or obscuring dialog. Do not launch while the guard is unresolved.

From the existing authenticated Web Client, activate the supported Designer-launch UI command used in EXP-009/R2 exactly once. Record that activation and its visible result. Keep the original Designer and Web Client open. Do not repeat the command or substitute another route after error, ambiguity, interruption or focus/reuse.

Prove with before/after browser identities plus inspected rendered evidence that one distinct additional Web Designer client appeared while the original Designer and Web Client remain present. A matching URL or focused existing window alone is insufficient. If the command only focuses/reuses the original client, creates an ambiguous surface or requests authentication, record the observed result and complete blocked rather than retrying. If any Mongoose Form unexpectedly appears/open in the additional Designer, record its visible identity and the discrepancy, then stop blocked without closing, manipulating or continuing it; do not repair the state or attribute its cause without evidence.

In the distinct additional Designer, complete only the normal launch-time User editing-scope confirmation if needed, visibly verify User scope and usable rendered Designer, and record its initial visible Form tabs/dialogs without opening any Form. Do not infer absence of hidden Forms, shared state or backend-session independence from an empty rendered surface. Require no unexpectedly open/inherited Mongoose Form on this rendered surface. If a Form appears before or after normal scope confirmation, capture the unexpected result and stop blocked without manipulating or closing it. The normal launch-time editing-scope dialog is distinct from a currently open runtime Form.

Read-only post-launch comparison must confirm the original Designer and authenticated Web Client are retained and the original Designer's inherited Form tabs, selected Form, scope, dirty-state indicators and dialogs match the AC-2 baseline. Capture inspected comparison evidence. If an inherited state changed unexpectedly, preserve observations, report the discrepancy and stop blocked without repair.

Final read-only audit must reconcile exactly one Web Client Designer-launch command activation, one distinct additional rendered client, only normal User scope confirmation if required, and a recorded rendered no-active-Web-Client-Form preflight, no unexpectedly open Form in the additional Designer, and zero Form openings, Form/component creations, property mutations, Saves, Form closes/reopens, client closures/restarts, authentication actions, unloads, Regenerates, preference changes or cleanup actions. Repository changes must be confined to the EXP-023 record and evidence/EXP-023/. A successful first execution supports only an observed additional-client launch procedure with inherited state preserved; it does not establish Caption recovery, persistence, backend-session independence or replay_verified status.

initial_instruction: EXP-023 tests only the prerequisite additional-Designer launch while retaining the original client. The new experiment record is expected to be missing: create it at the declared record path rather than repeatedly searching Git. Complete the bounded read-only AC-1/AC-2 preflight first, explicitly establishing that the authenticated Web Client has no currently open/active Mongoose Form. If a Form is open or that state is unresolved, stop blocked without changing it. Any Form unexpectedly appearing in the additional Designer is also a blocker; record it without closing or manipulating it. Preserve all inherited Form/dialog and dirty state. One launch-command activation is allowed after preflight; no artifact mutation, authentication, Form open/close, client closure, JavaScript browser inspection or alternative launch route is allowed. Report the task result to the coordinator and stop. A successful launch is not evidence of Caption recovery.
notes: Revised after specialist verdict objects on EXP-023-proposal-review. The earlier draft combined Caption recovery with an unverified additional-client launch while the original Designer stayed open, violating the one-new-capability rule. EXP-023 now tests that launch prerequisite alone, with no Caption or other artifact mutation. EXP-009/R2 verified a different lifecycle that closed the old Designer before new-client launch; their supported Web Client UI route is reused, but whether it creates an additional client while the original remains open is unverified until observed here. Inherited state from blocked EXP-021-R4 and EXP-022 must remain untouched. A later separately reviewed Caption experiment may use this launch procedure only after its required knowledge qualification is established. This draft remains unapproved pending specialist recheck. Added the no-active-Web-Client-Form guard and unexpected-Form blockers from specialist EXP-023-recheck (verdict objects). The linked Infor launch page confirms new tab/window launch but does not state current-Form auto-opening; that product behavior remains unverified here rather than being treated as an established fact. The rendered precondition keeps this experiment within its zero-Form-opening scope. Revised draft remains unapproved pending review.
